messages:
incident-bot: PAGED: high error rate observed for kv-prefix-cache in prod-eu — error-rate > 5% over 120s. Paging oncall @eng-sre. incident_id=INC-2026-3421

Sam L: oncall (sam) here, digging in. What's the customer impact? seeing 5xx from frontends?

Maria T: watching. Frontends show increased 502/503s for a subset of tenants (mostly EU). Cache prefix hit-rate fell sharply at ~2026-03-15T13:46Z. attaching quick stats: 

```
CacheSummary(prod-eu):
  window=5m
  hits=62123
  misses=35211
  hit_rate=63.7%  # baseline was ~98%
  miss_spike_start=2026-03-15T13:46:51Z
  miss_spike_peak=13:47:30Z
```

Maria T: logs snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T13:46:51Z prefix="user-msg" hit=false key=usr:12345:ctx:abcd latency=12ms
2026-03-15T13:47:02Z prefix="system" hit=false key=sys:init:efgh latency=3ms
2026-03-15T13:47:10Z backend_error=true code=503 svc=kv-backend-2
```

Kevin H: dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/cache/prod-eu?range=30m — you can see the hit-rate collapse aligned with a deploy at ~13:44. Also seeing increased KV backend tail latency.

Anya P: any recent deploys? Ops logs show a rollout of cache-proxy v2.9.1 at 2026-03-15T13:44:12Z (canary -> rollout). Might be related.

ops-bot: deploy: cache-proxy v2.9.1 rolled to prod-eu (initiated by ci/cd at 2026-03-15T13:44:12Z) — build 9f3b2c

Sam L: first hypothesis: cache-proxy change introduced a key-normalization or prefix hashing change -> increased key fragmentation -> KV reuse dropped -> backend load + 5xx. Alternatives: TTL change, eviction bug, or bad LRU interaction.

Sam L: immediate mitigation options: rollback to v2.9.0, manually rewarm hot prefixes, or bump TTL for prefixes to reduce misses. Which is fastest?

Maria T: rollback approval requires eng-runtime signoff. Warmup is fast and low-risk. I can run a warmup for top prefixes now. Also suggest temporarily increasing prefix TTL to 30s (from 5s) as stopgap.

Kevin H: ran warmup against top-200 prefixes for heavy tenants (commands run from debug node):
```
# warmup hot prefixes
for p in $(cat /tmp/hot-prefixes-top200.txt); do 
  curl -s -X POST "https://internal-cache/proxy/warm?prefix=$p" >/dev/null
done
# check cache stats after warm
curl -s https://internal-cache/proxy/stats | jq '.namespaces["prod-eu"].prefixes[0:10]'
```

Kevin H: after ~7m of warmup hit_rate climbed to ~91% and backend 5xx dropped. Partial recovery noted at 13:59Z.

Anya P: I'm collecting per-tenant KV-reuse counters and key-shard histograms to see if hashing distribution changed. Pulling diff between 2.9.0 and 2.9.1 config next.

Sam L: Sam -> If warmup holds, let's avoid immediate rollback. But prepare rollback plan (fast path) if we see regression again after TTL normalized. Also need to capture a full timeline and attach logs to RCA.

Maria T: here's the quick timeline I'm pasting into the incident doc: 
- 13:44:12 UTC — cache-proxy v2.9.1 rollout started (canary -> prod)
- 13:46:51 UTC — prefix miss spike begins (hit-rate drop)
- 13:47:30 UTC — backend 5xx/503s peak for certain tenants
- 13:52:10 UTC — warmup of top prefixes initiated
- 13:59:00 UTC — hit-rate back up to ~91% (partial recovery)
- 14:05:00 UTC — TTL bump applied to prefix layer (5s -> 30s)
- 14:10:30 UTC — backend error rate returned to baseline

Kevin H: raw metric excerpt (per-minute): 
```
2026-03-15T13:45:00Z hit_rate=97.9
2026-03-15T13:46:00Z hit_rate=85.2
2026-03-15T13:47:00Z hit_rate=63.7
2026-03-15T13:48:00Z hit_rate=58.4
2026-03-15T13:52:00Z hit_rate=72.5
2026-03-15T13:59:00Z hit_rate=91.0
```

Anya P: config diff snippet between 2.9.0 and 2.9.1 shows a change in key normalization routine: replaced `normalize_keys()` call with `normalize_keys_v2()` which includes trimming and hash-salt reorder. Suspect salt reordering yields different key shapes.

Sam L: marking hypothesis: key-normalization regression -> key fragmentation -> decreased KV reuse -> backend overload -> 5xx. Confidence: high-ish based on timeline + deploy.

David R: taking second-shift handoff now (David here). I'll own the incident from here. Handoff notes: warmup + TTL bump in place, hit-rate stable ~>90%. Preparing rollback playbook if we see another drop within 30m. Will notify eng-runtime and schedule a post-incident RCA. @Sam L please add any outstanding asks.

Sam L: thx @David R. Outstanding: archive full kv-backend logs for 13:40-14:15, export prefix histograms, and collect test vectors showing normalization differences. Also need customer-impact list (tenants affected + tickets).

Maria T: export started: s3://incidents/INC-2026-3421/logs/export-13_40-14_15.tar.gz (will upload ~15m)

ops-bot: created incident doc: https://docs.internal/incidents/INC-2026-3421 — added timeline and actions.

David R: action items (owned):
- [ ] Confirm whether normalize_keys_v2() is intended for prod (Anya)
- [ ] If unintended, coordinate rollback with eng-runtime (David + Sam)
- [ ] Prepare RCA skeleton and smoke tests to validate key-normalization (Anya + Kevin)
- [ ] Postmortem meeting scheduled tomorrow 10:00 UTC (invite will follow)

Anya P: I'll diff the library and open PR to revert the normalization if tests fail. Also creating a small unit test harness to generate hot-prefix distribution and assert reuse ratio.

Kevin H: note: warmup script and TTL bump are temporary mitigations. Need to consider better gradual rollout and canary validation for key-shaping changes. Recommend adding a KV-reuse regression alert to CI.

Sam L: agreed. Also capture runbook edits: add 'verify-pfx-reuse' step to release checklist for cache-proxy.

David R: handing off monitoring & ops to oncall rotation: @Anya P will follow up tonight. If anything flares before 14:45 UTC, page me immediately (pager duty). I'm marking this thread as the canonical incident channel.

Sam L: :thumbsup: Good work. I'll update the incident doc with the warmup commands and timeline.

Maria T: final note before I sign off: tenant list affected (high-impact): acme, globex, nova — support tickets created for each.

David R: logging handoff complete. I'll reconstruct a full timeline and start RCA draft. Please drop any additional logs in the incident doc.

ops-bot: incident INC-2026-3421 moved to status: mitigated -> monitoring

David R: (closing note) Root-cause hypothesis: key-normalization change in cache-proxy v2.9.1 caused key fragmentation and loss of KV cache reuse. Mitigations: warmup + TTL bump; next step rollback if observed regression; long-term: stricter canary tests and CI reuse alerts. I'll post a follow-up summary and link to the RCA doc when ready.
